newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS-Vendex profit rises, demerger on track.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Vendex profit rises, demerger on track.

text.p: Dutch retailing and services group Vendex International reported a 30 percent jump in net profits to 539 million guilders ($277 million) on Tuesday, and further detailed plans to demerge the company in two separate arms.
The headline profits were in line with expectations, but operating profit excluding income from the development and sale of property was just below forecasts at 362 million guilders.
Vendex said it intended to place and list shares worth 600 million guilders of the new group Vedior N.V. by an initial public offering (IPO) in the middle of 1997.
"Neither the figures nor their breakdown came as a surprise," Dennis Jullens, analyst at ING Barings said.
"On the demerger, I am positive," he added.
MeesPierson analyst Jurgen Veenker agreed, adding he was keen to get more details on the merger.
Hessels said he was confident the planned demerger of the services activities from Vendex's retailing core, announced in January, would work out positively for both arms.
"After the demerger, both companies will have a very strong position for further growth," he said.
After the IPO, Vendex's current shareholders will receive the remaining Vedior shares as soon as technically possible, Hessels said, adding this would likely take at least 90 days.
He said the demerger was going according to the plan, but the company was still awaiting government approval of the law permitting such operations.

"We expect the split-up to be finalised at the beginning of 1998, depending on the moment at which changes in the law on the split up of legal entities will become valid, or the obtaining of an earlier ruling by the Ministry of Finance," Vendex earlier said in a statement.
Hessels said the demerger would help Vendex's food retail unit pursue further acquisitions, mainly in the Netherlands.
"There's only a limited number of players on the market. We are now better positioned for further growth."

The group recently strengthened its foothold in the specialty stores segment with the acquisition of sports footware and clothing chain Scapino and the opticians chain of the Optische Exploitatie Maatschappij.
Operating income of the retail activities rose 29 percent to 352 million guilders. Excluding property income, it was up 50 percent to 247 million guilders.
Within the retail trade division, the food group increased its 'pure' operating income (excluding property) by 39 percent to 117 million guilders.
Longer opening hours in the Netherlands gave a push to turnover at the specialty and department stores.

Department stores also benefited from favourable fashion business pushing the 'pure' operating income at the department stores 75 percent higher to 56 million guilders. At Vendex's specialty stores it was up 51 percent to 74 million guilders.
The future Vedior business services arm increased operating profit excluding property by 14 percent to 129 million guilders.
It focuses on commercial cleaning and temporary employment.
Within the division, temporary employment operating income was up 19 percent at 75 million guilders in 1996/1997.

French temp employment agency BIS, acquired earlier this year, posted a 106 million franc loss in 1996, but Vendex board member Gert Smit said results had been positive during the first two months of 1997.
"We expect BIS to give a positive contribution to the group's results in 1997," Hessels said.
Once demerged, Vedior aims for cross-border expansion in order to be able to compete for major international customers, board member Gert Smit said.
A major player has to be present in all big European countries in order to be able to offer major contracts, he said.

Vendex announced a dividend of two guilders, up from 1.50 a year ago and repeated a previous profit forecast for the year ahead, saying it aimed to maintain an annual average profit rise of at least 10 percent.
MeesPierson's Veenker said he was positive on Vendex's prospects.
"Its markets look good. Consumer spending goes in the right direction, temporary employment does well and the French market seems to recover," he said.

He said the figures released today did not give him a reason to upgrade his forecasts for Vendex's core businesses, but added the contribution of property-related income would be above his earlier expectations.
Hessels said property-related income, 111 million guilders of the operating profit in 1996/97, would remain substantial for the next couple of years and at least equal last year's in 1997/98.
"I'll have to pencil in a higher contribution from real estate, since I had it at 80 million guilders for 1997/98," Veenker said.
Vendex shares closed two guilders higher at 92.90 guilders after peaking at 93.30 in a booming market.
($ = 1.945 Dutch Guilders)
